newsitem.title: CAMBODIA: Cambodia deputies to debate royal dissidents, ASEAN.
newsitem.headline: Cambodia deputies to debate royal dissidents, ASEAN.

text.p: A panel of legislators met on Thursday and called more talks on Friday on Cambodia's bid to join ASEAN and co-Premier Prince Norodom Ranariddh's request to expel dissident royalist MPs.
Ranariddh twinned the issues on Monday, saying Cambodia's request to join the Association of Southeast Asian Nations would be stalled until dissident MPs in his FUNCINPEC party were ousted.
The permanent committee of Cambodia's national assembly held a working meeting and agreed to convene again on Friday.

Sina Than, secretary general of the assembly, told reporters outside the office of parliament chief Chea Sim that the panel agreed to submit to an expert committee the documentation needed to join ASEAN.

Parliament has been stalled for several weeks in a row between Ranariddh's royalist party and the Cambodian People's Party (CPP) of co-Premier Hun Sen over a challenge to the prince's leadership from within his party.
A regular session from April 21 was postponed leading to concern that the assembly would not be able to pass 19 pieces of legislation covering membership of ASEAN.
The member nations of ASEAN -- Brunei, Indonesia, Malaysia, the Philippines, Singapore, Thailand and Vietnam -- have said they will admit Burma, Cambodia and Laos at the same time.
It was expected that they would be admitted in July but ASEAN officials have said the political problems in Cambodia could jeopardise this.
Ranariddh said on Monday that Cambodia's ASEAN bid would be stalled until eight dissident MPs in his party were expelled from parliament. Hun Sen and the CPP have opposed this.
The permanent committee in 1995 set a precedent by expelling current opposition leader and former FUNCINPEC member, Sam Rainsy, from parliament.
Sina Than said the committee would discuss Ranariddh's request to change the eight FUNCINPEC members but it was not clear if a vote would be taken.

Meanwhile, FUNCINPEC Secretary of State for Interior Ho Sok, said in a radio broadcast on Thursday the secretary general's office urged all members throughout the country not to take part in a planned May 31 congress by the royalist dissidents.
FUNCINPEC veteran Toan Chay, leader of the breakaway group, has said he plans to hold the congress then and that it could challenge Ranariddh's leadership of the party.

Hun Sen's support for the dissidents, who broke from Ranariddh in mid-April, has exacerbated poor relations between the two leaders, who formed an uneasy coalition government after U.N.-run elections in 1993.
